clue.text: Harmonise with Liberal breaking wind

indicators.note: something breaking another splits it open and sits in the middle of it

parts.note: a road or river winds, or bends

explanation.surface: A politician tries to keep the peace while breaking wind, an undignified moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' rhymes with 'kind' here: to wind is to bend.
explanation.definitionFit: To blend voices or colours is to make them sit together pleasingly, which is what harmonising does.

clue.text: One who's crashed might be covered with it

definitions.text: One who's crashed might be covered with it

parts.note: surface reading: a crash victim, perhaps covered with a sheet
setter's reading: crashed means fallen into bed asleep, so the cover is bedding

explanation.walkthrough: 'Crashed' suggests a car accident; it is slang for going to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedspread is the decorative top cover on a bed, laid over a sleeper.

clue.text: No time for fear? That's a mistake!

indicators.note: no means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone scolds another for being scared, calling it a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a wrong action or judgement, a slip or blunder.

clue.text: Curse someone like Bojo, being critical

parts.note: Bojo is Boris Johnson, a Conservative prime minister, so a Tory

explanation.surface: Swearing at Boris Johnson as a way of criticising him.
explanation.walkthrough: Bojo is a nickname for Boris Johnson, former UK Conservative prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnatory means expressing condemnation, so harshly disapproving.

clue.text: They produce small bloomers and S&M gear!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: plants, such as the cockspur hawthorn, that bear little flowers
second meaning: read as two words, spurs worn on a delicate part of the anatomy

explanation.surface: A cheeky line linking flowering plants with fetish equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' tempts you towards underwear, fitting the saucy surface, but here they are things that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockspur is the name of several plants, including a hawthorn, that bear flowers; split, the word suggests kinky spiked accessories.

clue.text: An old make of beer bottle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a long-established English brewery brand
second meaning: British slang for nerve or bravery

explanation.walkthrough: 'beer bottle' reads as one item; bottle is the second definition, British slang for nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage is a historic brewery name, and in British slang having bottle means having nerve or bravery.

clue.text: Share digs about old and rather grasping husband

parts.note: c. is short for circa, about
a bit means rather or somewhat

explanation.surface: A greedy old husband shares lodgings and grabs what he can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rather grasping husband' reads as clinging onto it: the second piece holds onto the husband's letter. Digs is British slang for lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohabit is to live together under one roof, sharing a home.

clue.text: Quiet place one might get a drop of whiskey

definitions.text: place one might get a drop of whiskey

explanation.surface: A peaceful spot for a nip of whiskey.
explanation.definitionFit: Still means calm and silent, and a still is the apparatus that distils spirits.

clue.text: Flag, having sex by the Dee?

parts.note: Jack Dee, the deadpan British comedian, so the first name of 'the Dee'

explanation.surface: A romantic encounter beside the River Dee.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee looks like the river; it is the comedian Jack Dee.
explanation.definitionFit: The Union Jack is the national flag of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: French scorer posed by exit with top off

indicators.note: taking off the top of a word removes its first letter

parts.note: sat for a portrait, i.e. posed
to die is to exit this life

explanation.surface: A French goalscorer strikes a pose as he leaves the field without his shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scorer' suggests football; here it is a composer, who writes scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Erik Satie was a French composer, and a composer writes musical scores.

clue.text: Bolt chops and port

parts.note: to bolt is to dart away
chops is slang for the mouth or jaws

explanation.surface: Reads like a menu or a set of instructions for a hasty meal of meat and a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt chops and port' looks like gobbling food and wine; chops are jaws, and port is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dartmouth is a harbour town in Devon, home of the Royal Navy college, so a port.

clue.text: Dope one I love gets in Delft on vacation

indicators.note: the earlier letters get in, so they go inside what follows
a word on vacation has emptied out its middle, keeping only its ends

parts.note: just the first and last letters of the Dutch town
love is nil, a zero in tennis

explanation.surface: A tourist confesses an affection while holidaying in the Dutch town of Delft.
explanation.walkthrough: IO sits inside the shell of Delft, all after the opening I for 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is a stupid person, the same as a fool or idiot in casual speech.

clue.text: Coat Lady Penelope's driver picked up

indicators.note: picked up as in heard, so we want something that sounds right rather than is spelt right

parts.note: Parker is the chauffeur of Lady Penelope in the TV puppet show Thunderbirds

explanation.surface: Lady Penelope's chauffeur picks up a coat for her.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the chauffeur's surname and the coat sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded, padded waterproof jacket, a kind of outdoor coat.

clue.text: What one might need after dodgy Cuban meal

definitions.text: What one might need after dodgy Cuban meal

indicators.note: dodgy means unsound or suspect, so the letters are not in their right order

explanation.surface: A bad dinner in Havana leads to a hospital trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: a suspect meal could land you in an emergency vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: After serious food poisoning you might need an emergency vehicle to take you to hospital.

clue.text: One of a series of dopes I messed about on E

indicators.note: letters messed about with have been jumbled out of their order

parts.note: taken as written; also slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Some idiots fool around while high on ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: E sits on the end after the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is one instalment of a TV or radio serial, one of a series of programmes.

clue.text: Helplessly drunk and impotent

definitions.meaning: first meaning: from the British police phrase drunk and ...

explanation.surface: A man too drunk to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk and incapable' is a British legal charge, echoed by the clue's own 'drunk and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Incapable means unable to act, so powerless, and is used of someone too intoxicated to look after themselves.

clue.text: Leaderless unit on military vehicle or vessel

indicators.note: without a leader the word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A unit without its commander rides on a tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the shortened unit after the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankard is a large drinking mug, usually with a handle, so a vessel for beer.

clue.text: Very successful track for the Boss

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the person in charge

explanation.surface: A hit single for Bruce Springsteen, nicknamed the Boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Boss' points to Springsteen, but is simply the chief.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart-topping single is a number one, and the top person in an organisation is also called that.

clue.text: Fellow actors right to tour English town

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go all round it, so these letters surround the next one

parts.note: a don is a college fellow

explanation.surface: A troupe of actors setting off on tour round an English town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English town' looks like the definition, but English supplies a letter and town alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Doncaster is a town in South Yorkshire, famous for its racecourse.

clue.text: Rotten broadcast got rid of portly comic Peter?

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard over the air, so the sound matters

parts.words: got rid of portly comic Peter
parts.note: Peter Kay is a well-built British stand-up comedian; to remove him is to de-Kay

explanation.surface: A broadcaster drops a popular, rotund comedian, which some call a rotten decision.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Kay is a famous comedian from Bolton, England, known for his round build.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotten food or wood has gone bad through natural decomposition.

clue.text: A male dread possibly could be loss of sensation in member!

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible arrangement of the letters among many

explanation.surface: A man fears losing feeling in his manhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' hints at something ruder, but is simply a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead arm is a temporary numbness in the arm, often after a punch, and an arm is a limb or member.

clue.text: Hit relations, one's a dim provincial type

parts.note: to bump is to knock or hit

explanation.surface: Someone thumps family members and is called a dim country type.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumpkin is an awkward, unsophisticated person from the countryside, a yokel.

clue.text: Blooming keep going in the sack!

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed
to last is to keep going, endure

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry about staying the course in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' is a mild British euphemism for a curse word, like 'blasted'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild British expletives used to express annoyance, like darned.

clue.text: Leader of the pack with highest of hands?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the boss or most important person
second meaning, playful: a bunch of the fruit is called a hand, so the uppermost one on it

explanation.surface: Sounds like a card game, where the leader holds the best hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hands' suggests cards, but a hand is also a cluster of bananas growing together.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is informal slang for the most important person in a group, the chief.

clue.text: Bum President making you mad essentially

indicators.note: making one letter into another swaps it out
the essence of a word is its very centre

explanation.surface: A jibe at a president who drives people crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: The U in the president's name becomes A. 'Bum' here is a vagrant, not a backside.
explanation.definitionFit: A bum, in American usage, is a homeless vagrant, which is what a tramp is.

clue.text: Those leading around stockcar track ram another car

indicators.note: those at the front of each word are their first letters

explanation.surface: A stock car race where front-runners ram rival cars.
explanation.definitionFit: The Astra is a Vauxhall and Opel family hatchback, a model of car.

clue.text: Additional old paintings must be brought round

indicators.note: brought round means turned about, so the word runs the other way

explanation.surface: More old paintings need to be fetched for an exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extra is more than the usual amount, an additional item.

clue.text: Drink brought round when? For this, perhaps

definitions.text: Drink brought round when? For this, perhaps

indicators.note: brought round something means wrapped around it

explanation.surface: Someone asks when the drinks are being served, and the answer is: for the celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue is the occasion when drinks are passed round.
explanation.definitionFit: A toast is a moment when glasses are raised and drunk in someone's honour.

clue.text: A pair of bishops could have books for him

definitions.text: A pair of bishops could have books for him

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, doubled

explanation.surface: Two bishops bring books along for a senior churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a monastery head is the sort of churchman bishops might supply with scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbot is head of a monastery, a cleric who would deal with bishops and read holy books.

clue.text: Drunk, so a truant and I get really high!

definitions.note: the answer speaks of itself in the first person

indicators.note: drunk letters stagger out of order

explanation.surface: A tipsy speaker and a school-skipping friend boast of getting very high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' looks like drugs or drink, fitting the truant; the speaker is really going to space.
explanation.definitionFit: Space travellers fly far above the Earth, higher than anyone else, so one could say this.

clue.text: Already heated new ward MEP tours starts to really explode

indicators.note: a new version of letters is a fresh arrangement of them
the starts of words are their opening letters

parts.note: the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A Euro-politician tours a hospital ward that is about to blow up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tours' is the link joining the MEP to the starts, which are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Prewarmed means heated beforehand, as an oven is before cooking.

clue.text: Come on over (gents getting naked for starters)

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its outer layer, so the outside letters go
turned over, so the word is flipped

explanation.surface: An invitation to come over, with men stripping off as an opener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for starters' puts the bracketed piece first.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to arrive inside a room or building is to come in, and 'come' alone can carry that sense.
